integrator_asks: src/patchtrace/unified/ir/pe_tables.py (other session's lane, not touched): the same PE-2 defect remains. _Rva.read (about line 150; cap at :27, use at :295) asks the reader for one over-size read, so a base-relocation directory between MAX_READ_BYTES (16 MiB) and MAX_RELOC_DIRECTORY (32 MiB) is swallowed as 'reloc-unreadable' with zero relocations. open_risks: PE-8: Ctx.warn keeps the first message per code, so a file with both an over-long name and a section-cut name shows only the first one's wording (true but incomplete). This is the existing rule for every code; the spec amendment states it.

PE-8: a name that runs to the end of the FILE without a terminator is still returned whole with no warning (unchanged and now pinned by a test). If the file boundary should also be reported, that changes status on such files and needs a decision.

PE-7 timing test is a relative bound (one ordinal <= 3 x one-name-per-ordinal, best of three; measured 6.5x before, about 0.9x after). The deterministic comparison-count test is the strict guard; the timing one could still flake on a heavily loaded runner.

PE-6: at a cap the parser now reads one more entry; once the total-name cap is reached exactly, each later DLL costs one name read and one thunk read (bounded by the 512-DLL cap). An unbacked entry right after a cap now reports import_rva_out_of_file instead of an over-cap code.
